entities.summary:
The Prime Minister of Norway is the head of government of Norway and the most powerful person in Norwegian politics. The position was first established in 1814, with the adoption of the Norwegian Constitution. This entity is significant because it represents the culmination of Norway's struggle for independence from Denmark and Sweden. The Prime Minister is also a key figure in Norwegian politics, responsible for forming and leading the government.

The role of the Prime Minister has evolved over time, with the position becoming increasingly powerful in the 20th century. Notable Prime Ministers include Johan Sverdrup, who introduced parliamentary rule in 1884, and Einar Gerhardsen, who played a key role in rebuilding Norway after World War II. The Prime Minister is also responsible for making key decisions on economic policy, foreign policy, and national security.

The legacy of the Prime Minister is far-reaching, with many of the country's key institutions and policies being shaped by the office. The Prime Minister is also a key figure in international relations, representing Norway on the world stage. Today, the Prime Minister remains a powerful symbol of Norwegian politics and identity.

As the Norwegian Prime Minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, once said, "The Prime Minister is the leader of the government and the main representative of the Norwegian people in international relations," emphasizing the significance of the role in Norwegian politics.
